subject: Linguistics
title: Egyptian Hieroglyphs
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Egyptian Hieroglyphs.

hook.text: For 1,500 years nobody could read hieroglyphs—until the Rosetta Stone was found in 1799.

buildup.text: Egyptian hieroglyphs mixed pictograms, logograms, and phonetic signs in one elaborate system.

discovery.text: Champollion cracked the code in 1822 by recognizing that hieroglyphs included phonetic spelling.

twist.text: Hieroglyphs weren't just pictures of things—many signs represented sounds, like an alphabet hidden inside.

climax.text: The system was used for over 3,000 years—from the pyramids to the Roman occupation of Egypt.

punchline.text: Pictures that talked—for over three millennia.

quiz.question: How did Champollion decode hieroglyphs?
options: By recognizing they included phonetic signs
